findings.why_it_matters: The section heading appears twice and the first copy sits on the Debug page XV-10, so a tool locating Section XVI by heading finds it on the wrong page.
findings.detail: Page 698 (XV-10) prints no Section XVI heading; the heading is printed on page 699, where the markdown also carries it as `# <u>SECTION XVI: SEGMENTATION MODULE</u>`. The copy at the end of page 698 is a stray duplicate.

findings.why_it_matters: 1.5 is a sibling of 1.1-1.4 (rendered ###) and 1.6 (###); at ## it outranks its parent `## 1.` siblings and breaks the outline.
findings.detail: Heading at the wrong level: should be `### 1.5 SEGMENTATION CLASSIFICATION` like `### 1.4 ORGANIZATION` and `### 1.6 SEGMENTATION CONTROL`.

findings.why_it_matters: 2.3 is a sibling of 2.2 (rendered ### on page 702); at ## with its subclauses at ### the outline places the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause at the level of `2. ENVIRONMENT DIVISION`.
findings.detail: Should be `###`, and its 2.3.1-2.3.4 subheadings `####` (rendered `###`), matching 2.2 / 2.2.1-2.2.4 on page 702.

findings.why_it_matters: The level-2 box marks the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause as a level-2 (Segmentation level 2) feature; GR 2 and 3 without the marker read as level-1 rules.
findings.pdf_says:
(2) Those segments having segment-numbers from the segment-limit through 49 are considered as overlayable fixed segments.

(3) When the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause is omitted, all segments having segment-numbers from 0 through 49 are considered as permanent segments of the object program.
findings.markdown_says:
(2) Those segments having segment-numbers from the segment-limit through 49 are considered as overlayable fixed segments.

(3) When the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause is omitted, all segments having segment-numbers from 0 through 49 are considered as permanent segments of the object program.
findings.detail: The printed box encloses the whole of 2.3 through the end of general rule (3). The markdown wraps every other paragraph of 2.3 in ║ level-2 markers but leaves general rules (2) and (3) unmarked.

findings.why_it_matters: The general format of the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause is inside the printed level-2 box; unmarked, the format reads as level 1.
findings.detail: The general format lies inside the box that encloses all of 2.3; the markdown figure carries no level-2 box marker (page 702's boxed OBJECT-COMPUTER format uses ╔ ║ ╚ marks for the same purpose).

findings.why_it_matters: 3.3 is a sibling of 3.1 and 3.2 (both ###); at ## it ranks with `## 3. PROCEDURE DIVISION IN THE SEGMENTATION MODULE`.
